excluded_evidence.quote: The MODIS Airbourne Simulator (MAS) is a modified Daedalus Wildfire scanning spectrometer which flies on a NASA ER-2 and provides spectral information similar to that provided by the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS)

suite: MetadataAssociation PARENT → 'MAS' version 0 does not resolve to a CMR collection (versions in CMR: none); 'MAS' is the instrument name.
Linked page could not be reached from this environment (ConnectTimeout): https://mas.arc.nasa.gov/reference.html
Linked page could not be reached from this environment (ConnectTimeout): https://mas.arc.nasa.gov/
Linked page could not be reached from this environment (ConnectTimeout): https://mas.arc.nasa.gov/data/srf/ARC-Jun95/msr0695.ph

The data set document gives no processing information: sections 3, 5, 6, 9 and 10 read "Information not available at this time", and the Instrument and Calibration sections refer to the "MAS User's Guide", which is not linked.
The README sample output (global attributes) shows CalibrationVersion "SCAR-B King 1.0" and CreationDate 1996, i.e. it was taken from a SCAR-B file, not a SCAR-A one.
The README describes the files as netCDF read with HDF libraries; the abstract and data set document say HDF/netCDF. The granules (e.g. scara_mas_930712.003) have no file extension.
The title and abstract call MAS the "Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectrometer (MODIS) Airborne Simulator" (MODIS is a Spectroradiometer) and contain typos ("Airbourne", "the the", "was was").
ProcessingLevel 1B is described as 'Calibrated from Level 0 raw radiance', but no Level 0 collection or calibration version is identified.
MASL1B 1 at LAADS claims 1993–2007 coverage but has no granules for the SCAR-A period; the SCAR-A MAS data are not part of it.
